messages:
Anna L: Quick heads-up — ran into a nasty startup edgecase in the sample app when both REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_PROJECT_TOKEN are present. App picks one silently and it's not obvious which. Repro steps: set both, `redwood init` -> app authenticates but hits permission errors later.

Mike O: Ugh seen that. SDK currently uses the first env it finds (order depends on process.env iteration) so nondeterministic across runtimes.

Sam K: That's bad. We should define deterministic precedence rather than relying on env enumeration. My proposal: REDWOOD_PROJECT_TOKEN (project-scoped) > REDWOOD_ORG_TOKEN (org-scoped) > REDWOOD_API_KEY (legacy global). That matches least-surprise for most customers.

Jess P: Agreed on precedence. Also worth adding a startup warning if multiple tokens exist with different scopes. Something like: `WARN: multiple auth tokens detected, using REDWOOD_PROJECT_TOKEN. Remove duplicates to avoid accidental scope mismatch.`

Anna L: +1 for warning. Another related issue: during key rotation CI jobs sometimes see 401s for a few seconds and then succeed. SDK retries treat 401 as non-retryable so user-visible failures happen. Any ideas for rotation-safe behavior?

Sam K: We can add a small grace-window flow: if server returns 401 with header `x-redwood-rotation: pending`, SDK should retry once after 200ms. Also expose `rotateGrace` opt in SDK config so enterprise customers can tune.

Mike O: Careful with retries — double billing for token use isn't a big issue for us, but we should avoid exponential retries on 401. Single short retry seems fine. Also log a specific telemetry event `auth.rotation.retry` so we can see how often rotations hit clients.

Jess P: For sample apps + quickstarts we should update README + env examples. Right now README shows both `REDWOOD_API_KEY` and `REDWOOD_PROJECT_TOKEN` in separate examples, which might encourage setting both. Change to show only the preferred project-scoped example and call out migration.

Anna L: I'll open a tiny PR with: 1) deterministic precedence code (explicit order), 2) startup warning if >1 different-scope token present, 3) add single-retry-on-401-if-rotation-header, and 4) README tweak. Any objections?

Mike O: No objections. Can we also add a small unit test that simulates env ordering differences (node vs deno) so this doesn't regress?

Sam K: Good call. Add e2e test with a fake auth server that returns `x-redwood-rotation: pending` then 200 after retry.

Jess P: I'll update the quickstart snippets after the PR lands. Also create a short dev-ex note for docs team so they can reflect the change in onboarding flows.

ci-bot: build triggered for branch anna/project-token-precedence (CI: #4521) :blue_circle:

Anna L: Thanks all — aiming to ship this week. If anyone wants to pair on the tests ping me.
